override_text: Kc4 walks into Qe2+. Your king has to retreat to b3, far from the action. Kc2 keeps the king safer.
coach_note: Endgame king-positioning blunder. Walks into a tempo-losing check; future detector: walked_into_check_demotion.

override_text: Nf3 was the natural square. Nge2 puts the knight where it blocks your bishop on g2. From f3 the knight controls e5 and supports the centre.
coach_note: Wrong development square. Positional, not a clean detector — coach override.

override_text: Their bishop on e4 was aimed at h7, right next to your king. After they sacrifice with check, you take with the king and their queen swings to h5 with check. Their queen ends up winning your queen on g5. g6 blocks the diagonal and stops the whole thing.
coach_note: Greek Gift defense. walked_into_attack detector exists but didn't fire here because pv_after_played in the V5 record is only one move long. Investigate why Stockfish output isn't preserving the multi-ply line.

override_text: Nxc5 wins the bishop on c5. Your knight on a4 was already there, attacking it. Qf3 misses the free piece.
coach_note: Missed capture — but knight (3) takes bishop (3), equal trade. cp_loss came from missing the only good move in a bad position. Captured == moving so my detector skipped it.

override_text: c4 was the move. Pushing the c-pawn closes the queenside and slows their attack on your king. Qe3 doesn't address what they are building.
coach_note: Defensive pawn break. Hard to template — coach override.

override_text: Re2 attacks their queen on f2. They have to move it, and you reach a winning position. g4 weakens your own king instead.
coach_note: Missed attack on enemy queen (not a capture, but a forced threat). Future detector: missed_attack_on_queen — best move attacks an enemy queen, queen has to move.

override_text: Qe8 was needed to defend along the back rank. f6 weakens your king and opens lines white wanted opened. The knight on h6 stays vulnerable.
coach_note: Defensive prophylaxis. Hard to template generically.

override_text: Nd4+ was the killer. The knight to d4 checks your king and forks the white queen on a5. After their forced king move, you take the queen. Qf5+ throws the position away.
coach_note: Missed combination ending in winning the queen via fork after check. Should be caught by combination_chain when pv_after_best is populated; investigate why pv_after_best is empty here.

override_text: Bf5 defends h7 along the diagonal. The white queen on h4 was eyeing your king, and Re8 doesn't address it. Bf5 stops the attack before it starts.
coach_note: Defensive prophylaxis (defend a king-side square).

override_text: Nd6+ was the move. The knight check forces their king to move, and you keep your winning attack. Kc3 walks into checks instead.
coach_note: Missed check — should be caught by missed_check detector once deployed.

override_text: Kh1 was needed first. Their knight on f4 attacks your pawn on g2 and your king on g1. Ne3 lets the knight come in. Kh1 steps out of the way.
coach_note: Prophylactic king move (avoid impending threats). Specialized — coach override.

override_text: Bxh7 wins the pawn next to their king. Your bishop on g8 takes for free and opens up the king's cover. Qg7 misses the simpler win.
coach_note: Missed capture — should be caught by missed_capture detector once deployed.

override_text: d4 challenges the centre right away. h3 wastes a move on the side and lets their pieces settle. In the opening, every move should fight for the centre or develop a piece.
coach_note: Opening principle violation. Hard to template per-position.

override_text: Ne4 was the active square. The knight to e4 challenges their pieces in the centre. Bc4 doesn't address their strong knight on d4.
coach_note: Positional — better square for a piece. Stays as coach override.

override_text: Bxf6 was right. Trading the bishop for their knight doubles their pawns and weakens their king side. Bh4 keeps the bishop but lets them recapture cleanly.
coach_note: Missed_capture-like (gxf6 doubles pawns). Captures knight (3) with bishop (3) — equal trade by raw value, but the structural damage matters. Detector should consider 'doubling enemy pawns' as a value bonus.

override_text: Nxg3 wins the bishop on g3. Your knight on e4 takes for free, then their h-pawn or f-pawn recaptures and gives them broken pawns near their king. h5 just weakens your own king.
coach_note: Equal-piece capture (knight=3, bishop=3) where the value comes from doubling enemy pawns. missed_capture detector skipped this because captured_value == moving_value. Future refinement: bonus value when capturing piece is defended by king-side pawns (hxg3 or fxg3 doubles).

override_text: a6 attacks their queen on b5. They have to move the queen, and you keep your structure. Kb8 doesn't address the queen.
coach_note: Missed attack on enemy queen (pawn attack). Build missed_attack_on_queen detector — best move attacks the enemy queen.

override_text: Qe2 was needed to defend the second rank. Their queen and rook were lined up to attack — Qe2 covers it. Rfd1 leaves the defence light.
coach_note: Defensive piece coordination. Hard to template.

override_text: b5 attacks the white bishop on c4. The bishop has to move, and you gain time. Bxe4 trades your active bishop for a knight.
coach_note: Missed pawn attack on bishop. Same family as a6 vs queen — build missed_attack_on_piece (pawn attacks higher-value enemy piece).

override_text: Nd7 develops the last piece. From d7 the knight defends your king side and supports the centre. h5 weakens your king and opens lines for their queen.
coach_note: Development-vs-king-safety in middlegame. Coach override.

override_text: exf6 was the move. The pawn capture opens lines toward their king and supports your queen on e6. exd6 closes the attack.
coach_note: Massive cp_loss — likely throws away mate. Specific tactical case; the detector for this is combination_chain once pv_after_best is populated.

override_text: Be4 attacks their knight on f3. The bishop is more active there and forces them to respond. Ne3 walks the knight into a worse square.
coach_note: Better-active-square for a piece. Coach override.

override_text: Ref7 brings your rook to the seventh rank. From f7 it attacks their pieces and supports your king. Kf7 just shuffles the king without a plan.
coach_note: Rook activation / piece reorganization. Coach override.

override_text: Kf6 was needed. Your king must walk forward to support your pawns. Rb1 takes the rook off the back rank but loses the winning idea — your king staying back lets their pawn run.
coach_note: Endgame king activation. cp_loss=9022 because Rb1 abandons the winning king-march plan. Coach override.
